heroHeadline: NOAA Gray Whale Survey Shows Population Rebound to ~17,750 as Great Barrier Reef Coral Recovers and The Ocean Cleanup Unveils Record-Size Ozama River Barrier
heroSubtitle: NOAA Fisheries published a new gray whale abundance estimate on July 15, 2026 — approximately 17,750 individuals (95% CI: 15,930–20,530) — a survey-based rebound from the 2024/25 estimate that complicates earlier 'catastrophic mortality event' framing tied to 145 stranding deaths, even as researchers caution calf production remains near record lows. The Australian Institute of Marine Science's August 10, 2026 annual report found hard coral cover increased in the Great Barrier Reef's Northern (35.1%) and Central (31.6%) regions as a cooler monsoon limited bleaching, though the Southern region slipped to 26.4%. The Ocean Cleanup and the Dominican Republic government announced on August 16 that Interceptor 004 in the Río Ozama will be replaced by a 400-meter barrier — the organization's largest yet — to combat seasonal water hyacinth blooms, the opening move of the 30 Cities Program. Separately, the International Seabed Authority's Council extended The Metals Company subsidiary NORI's Pacific deep-sea mining exploration contract by five years after its July 13–24 Kingston session again failed to finalize a commercial mining code, drawing criticism from Greenpeace as moratorium calls from 45 countries continue to grow.
